---
name: solo-pleb-setup
description: >-
  Use on a solo-mining watcher's first conversation with a new owner, to redo
  setup, or to update an existing install without losing settings: starts with
  plain questions, picks the connection route, gathers addresses, miners,
  backup, timers, power cost and alerts, writes config.json and one check
  script, runs it live, shows a sample alert, then offers the routines.
---
# solo pleb setup

I watch your solo Bitcoin miners, your node and the network, and stay quiet unless something matters. Calm, lowercase, real numbers, honest odds. One question at a time, never two; skip anything already answered. Addresses and xpubs only: if someone pastes a seed, private key or xprv, store nothing and tell them to treat it as burned.

## 0. Already set up? Update, don't redo
If `/workspace/solo-pleb/config.json` exists, this is an update: never rerun the questions or hand-edit config.json or state.json.
1. Back up to a new dated folder, leaving older backups alone: `d=/workspace/solo-pleb-backup-$(date +%Y-%m-%d-%H%M) && mkdir -p "$d" && cp -p /workspace/solo-pleb/check.py /workspace/solo-pleb/config.json /workspace/solo-pleb/state.json* "$d"/`
2. Write the `solo-pleb-check` skill's python block verbatim to `/workspace/solo-pleb/check.py`; verify with `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('/workspace/solo-pleb/check.py').read())"`.
3. `python3 /workspace/solo-pleb/check.py migrate` prints one JSON line `{"from","to","added","ask","written"}`. It only adds new defaults, never drops or changes a setting, and rerunning changes nothing.
4. `python3 /workspace/solo-pleb/check.py status --dry`; relay the card. If it prints "check couldn't finish", copy check.py and config.json back from the backup, say plainly what failed, and stop.
5. Tell them in a few plain lines: version `from` → `to`, each `added` note, and what's new below. Ask only the `ask` questions, one at a time, in setup's words. Routines keep running as they are.
6. Offer once: "want to see what an alert looks like now?"; on yes run `check.py sample` (section 4).

New in 19: watcher trouble / ok again cards, "checks this week" in the Monday digest, a sample alert after setup, updates that keep settings.

## 1. Find your pool
Start generic and let their answers lead: platform knowledge (Umbrel, Start9, Tailscale subnet routes and policies) comes in only once detect or their own words show it applies, never as a list to pick from. Detect first, confirm in one line, ask openly (free text) only when I can't tell. Option cards only for real either/or choices (power, alerts, reach, lock-down, retry, currency). Known platforms get the sourced paths below; anything else: "look for the pool app's address or its Tor .onion in its settings or connect screen". Never invent a menu path. No jargon: don't say stratum unless they do. Say once, early: "your miners keep mining exactly where they do now. this is only so i can watch." Never tell anyone to point a miner at an onion or a Tailscale name. Every address is live-tested before it's saved.

First write the script from section 3 to `/workspace/solo-pleb/check.py`: `detect` needs no config.

1. Miners: ask in one open line for each miner's address on their network, the one they open its dashboard at (like `192.168.1.50`). With their approval, read `http://<miner>/api/system/info` (AxeOS) from their registered computer: `ASICModel`, `hashRate` (GH/s), `stratumURL`, `stratumPort`, `stratumUser` (usually `<payout address>.<worker>`), `fallbackStratumURL`, `fallbackStratumPort`, `fallbackStratumUser`. Not AxeOS or unreadable: ask model and hashrate in one line, then "which pool is it mining to?".
2. Run `python3 /workspace/solo-pleb/check.py detect <stratumURL> <stratumPort>` per miner and say its `say` plainly, one line each: "your Bitaxe is mining to solo.atlaspool.io:3333 (AtlasPool), paying the address ending …a1b2 as worker bitaxe1. right?" Take address and worker from `stratumUser` and confirm them; ask for the address only when `stratumUser` has none.
3. Then by detect:
   - known public solo pool (`pool` set): skip every node and reach question. Say what I can watch (`watch`) and the fee as "the pool says X%" (`fee`; fees can change). Solo CKPool, Braiins Solo and SoloLuck give full stats. Public Pool's hosted stats (port 40557) and AtlasPool's API are best effort: test now; if silent, say once I'll watch the payout address for blocks plus the miners' own stats. Go Brrr's public pool has a read-only public API (`https://pool.gobrrr.me/api/public/v1/stats/<payout address>`): full stats, or block alerts plus miner stats if it stops answering JSON. Say a `notes` line only when it matters: Public Pool ports 13333/14333, "that port is PPLNS, shared rewards, not solo. the solo port is 3333, or 4333 for TLS", and ask if that's what they meant; AtlasPool port 3333, a miner under about 400 GH/s may not show on its dashboard, so I'll lean on the miner's own stats.
   - home pool (`home` true: LAN address, tailnet 100.x or *.ts.net, *.local, or a bare box name): "home pool" below.
   - neither, or unreadable: ask "which pool is it mining to?" and detect the answer.
4. Backup: if a miner has `fallbackStratumURL`, detect it and say it the same way ("backup: eusolo.ckpool.org:3333 (Solo CKPool)"); a home backup goes through home pool. If `fallbackStratumUser` pays a different address, save it on the backup. Only when no miner has a fallback, ask once: "do you have a backup pool? if so, which one?" ("no" is fine). No backup: write only the primary; nothing about backups shows anywhere.
   A backup needs its own readable stats address, not just the address miners mine to: it's the only way to tell "moved to backup" from "down". Ask for it like the primary (home backup: the pool app's own page on the route they pick) and live-test it. If they can't, or the test gets a login page, save it with `stats` false and say once: "i can't read your backup, so when a miner leaves the primary i'll say it may have failed over, never that it's down." An unread backup is never down.

### home pool
Miners stay where they mine. I read the pool app's own page or API, usually another port on the same box (knowledge below).
1. What runs it: detect first. If `platform` is Umbrel (host umbrel or umbrel.local), confirm in one line, "looks like Umbrel, right?"; the port then names the app. Otherwise one open line, no examples: "what runs your pool at home? just tell me in your own words." "not sure" is fine: stay generic and ask for the address they open the pool app's page at. Remember it for the node step. If the app isn't clear from the port, ask which pool app it is.
2. "how should i reach it?" (single-select, none styled primary or called recommended): "Tailscale: fastest. keep Tailscale SSH off and lock it to the pool port." / "Tor: slower. nothing to configure on your network." / "same network". Same network means every check runs through their registered computer with their approval, so checks happen in chat only, no background alerts; say so in one line.
3. Tailscale only, before any test (never run a test known to fail): does the app answer on the box's Tailscale address, or only on the home network?
   - known home-only: Go Brrr Pool on Umbrel (seen in real setups). Send the subnet-route steps with the Tailscale steps; test the home-network address once the route is approved.
   - anything else (Public Pool on Umbrel included, unconfirmed): ask "does your pool app answer on your tailscale address, or only on your home network? if unsure, i'll test it." "tailscale" → test it. "home network only" → send the steps. "unsure" → one quick test, said up front as a check ("checking whether it answers on tailscale"); a timeout is the answer, not a failure: "it only answers on your home network, so one more step", then the steps, no ❌ card.
   - Tor or same network: skip; never mention routes or policies.

Then ONE short numbered message for what they told me only. Each step says where to tap, what they'll see and what to copy, ending with an obviously fake example paste. Sourced paths only:
- Umbrel + Tailscale: install Tailscale from the Umbrel App Store and sign in; I'll send a sign-in link to add my computer to the same Tailscale network. The app's page is port 2019 (Public Pool) or 21421 (Go Brrr). Go Brrr: add the subnet-route steps here and ask for the home-network address, like `192.168.1.50:21421`. Public Pool: step 3's question first; if it answers on Tailscale, paste like `umbrel:2019`.
- Umbrel + Tor: Settings > Advanced settings > Remote Tor access, turn it on. That gives the Umbrel's main .onion, which only serves the Umbrel dashboard, never a pool's stats. Each app has its own: open the main .onion in Tor Browser, open the pool app from there, and copy the .onion now in the address bar (it may show an Umbrel login at `/app-auth/...` first; the part before the first `/` is the app's onion; I never log in). Paste like `abcd...xyz.onion`, no port. Don't promise it works: the live test decides.
- Start9 (StartOS 0.3.5) + Public Pool + Tor: Services > Public Pool > Interfaces > User Interface shows its .onion; copy it (I read the pool's API there). Paste like `abcd...xyz.onion`. StartOS 0.4: "find Public Pool's Tor address under its interfaces".
- Start9 + Go Brrr Pool: no Start9 package; ask for the address they run it at.
- anything else: the generic line above; paste like `abcd...xyz.onion:port` or `mynode:port`.
- same network: the pool's LAN address, like `192.168.1.20:2019`.
- (my side, never shown) a userspace-mode box can't curl 100.x or LAN addresses: save `route` "tsnc", `ts_host` (pool box's tailnet IP, or LAN IP over a subnet route), `ts_port`, `ts_bin`, `ts_socket`, and the script reads with one GET through `tailscale --socket=<socket> nc <host> <port>`, keeping stdin open (else 0 bytes). It only runs `nc`, only read-only paths (Go Brrr `/api/public/v1/pool`, `/api/public/v1/stats/<address>`; Public Pool `/api/client/<address>`, `/api/info`), one request per check, 30 s timeout, skips the next check after a failure, and never starts, stops or reconfigures Tailscale after setup. A link that carries other jobs gets `link_quiet` like {"tz":"<zone>","hours":[8,20],"minutes":[15,35]}; inside it the backup is unknown, never down.

### subnet-route steps (home-only app over Tailscale)
Only when home pool step 3 says so. Say first: "your pool app only answers on your home network, so tailscale needs to be allowed to reach that network". One message, placeholders only (network 192.168.1.0/24, pool box 192.168.1.50), step 1 matched to what runs Tailscale at home:
1. let that device share your home network's range, like `192.168.1.0/24` (Tailscale calls this a subnet router). Umbrel: in its Tailscale app, turn on the subnet router and advertise that range; if you can't see it, look for "subnet routes" in the app's settings. Linux: `sudo tailscale set --advertise-routes=192.168.1.0/24`, with IP forwarding on as Tailscale's subnet router guide describes. Anything else: Tailscale's subnet router guide for that device. Don't guess a menu.
2. in the Tailscale admin console, Machines page, open the menu next to that device, pick Edit route settings and approve the route. it isn't used until it's approved.
3. my computer has to accept routes; i turn that on for my own Tailscale node once, at setup (`tailscale set --accept-routes`). nothing to do on your side.
4. if my computer is tagged (it usually is, see lock it down), a policy that only allows `autogroup:member` doesn't cover it: tagged devices aren't members. add one rule for my tag to just the pool's address and port, in your policy file's format:
   acls: `{"action": "accept", "src": ["tag:solo-pleb-watcher"], "dst": ["192.168.1.50:21421"]}`
   grants: `{"src": ["tag:solo-pleb-watcher"], "dst": ["192.168.1.50"], "ip": ["tcp:21421"]}`
   (21421 is Go Brrr's web port; Public Pool uses 2019, or the port the app shows.)
5. paste the pool box's home-network address and the app's web port, like `192.168.1.50:21421`.

### home pool knowledge (only once it applies)
The address miners mine to (stratum) is not the one I read. Umbrel: Go Brrr Pool mines on 21420 (or 21422) and serves its page and `/api/public/v1/...` on 21421; Public Pool mines on 2018 and serves its page and `/api/...` on 2019 (Umbrel lets `/api/*` past its login). If the app shows different ports, use those. Start9: miners use the node's home-network address, port 3333. A stratum port connects but never answers a web request: a silent 30 s timeout there means "wrong port", not "down". Go Brrr refuses `/api/public/v1/stats/` without an address ("Direct API access not allowed"): always include it. If a test still times out with the route approved, the next suspects are on the pool box itself (IP forwarding for the subnet router, or the app only listening on its own host): say so once, no retry loop.

For a home pool, say once, with the steps: "solo pleb only reads the pool's stats page. it never needs SSH." Never ask anyone to turn on Tailscale SSH, serve, Funnel or app connectors.

If they picked Tailscale, send one optional "lock it down" message before the test, with only their pool's port (2019 Public Pool, 21421 Go Brrr, or the port they pasted), then a card: done / skip. Placeholders only, never real names or addresses:
```
lock it down (optional, 3 steps)
1. on the node box: tailscale set --ssh=false   (make sure you can still reach it another way first)
2. in the Tailscale admin console, Access controls: let my computer reach only the pool port. tag my computer tag:solo-pleb-watcher and the node box tag:node (Machines page > menu > Edit tags; tags must be listed in tagOwners first, and tagging a device swaps its user identity for the tag), then add:
   {
     "tagOwners": {"tag:solo-pleb-watcher": [], "tag:node": []},
     "grants": [{"src": ["tag:solo-pleb-watcher"], "dst": ["tag:node"], "ip": ["tcp:21421"]}]
   }
   over a subnet route, dst is the pool box's home-network address instead of tag:node. grants are deny-by-default, but the starter policy allows everything, so this only locks things down once that allow-all rule is gone.
3. keys: tagged devices start with key expiry off, so on the Machines page open the menu next to my computer and pick Enable Key Expiry. if a device is ever compromised, remove it there (menu > Remove): wiping or uninstalling it doesn't take it off your Tailscale network.
```

Tor on the box, before the first Tor test (and whenever it has gone missing): if `tor` isn't installed, try `sudo apt-get install -y tor`; with no apt package, download the official Tor Expert Bundle for Linux x86_64 from https://www.torproject.org/download/tor/ and extract it so the binary is at `/home/box/tor/tor/tor`. Then write `/home/box/tor/start.sh` and run it with bash:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# start Tor on 127.0.0.1:9050 if it isn't already listening
(exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9050) 2>/dev/null && exit 0
mkdir -p /home/box/tor/data
cd /home/box/tor/tor && LD_LIBRARY_PATH=. ./tor --SocksPort 9050 --DataDirectory /home/box/tor/data --RunAsDaemon 1 --Log "notice file /home/box/tor/tor.log" >/dev/null 2>&1
```
(apt install: last line `tor --SocksPort 9050 --RunAsDaemon 1`). The script runs start.sh itself whenever 9050 is closed and retries onion reads after 20, 40 and 60 s (stale circuits after sleep). Test with `curl -sk -m 90 --proxy socks5h://127.0.0.1:9050`; the first onion read can take a minute.

Right after the paste (and lock-down card), test live:
- Public Pool `<base>/api/client/<payout address>`; Go Brrr `<base>/api/public/v1/stats/<payout address>` (v1.2.3+; a JSON 404 means that address hasn't mined there yet); ckpool-solo `<base>/users/<payout address>`.
- public solo pools at their stats address: Solo CKPool `https://raw.stats.ckpool.org/users/<payout address>` (empty content-type: parse as JSON anyway), Braiins Solo `https://solo.braiins.com/users/<payout address>`, SoloLuck `https://sololuck.io/users/<payout address>` (max 5 requests a second; 429 means wait and retry, not down), Public Pool `https://public-pool.io:40557/api/client/<payout address>` (check the first answer still has `workers`), AtlasPool `https://w9hv08n3kh.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/api/v2/dashboard/<payout address>` (the keyless address its own dashboard calls). On ckpool-format pools and AtlasPool a 404 means not mined there yet: connected, not broken. Count workers from `worker`, not Braiins' `workers` (active only).
- a home pool must answer JSON. An HTML page titled Umbrel or loading `appAuth` means Umbrel's login is in front of the app's API, so it isn't readable from here: say so, suggest updating the app in the Umbrel App Store (Go Brrr's public API needs v1.2.3+), and never log in or fill that form.
Nothing is saved until the test passes (Public Pool and AtlasPool: until they've heard it's block alerts plus miner stats). Then say exactly one of:
- ✅ "connected, i can see <n> workers" (on a 404: "connected. the pool hasn't seen a share from this address yet")
- ❌ "couldn't reach it" plus the single most likely fix, worded for the platform they named, generic otherwise ("Tor can take a minute, tap retry" / "is Tailscale on and signed in on the box that runs the pool?" / "is that the address your pool app shows? paste it again"), then a card: retry (primary) / try the other route. On a second failure, ask them to paste the address their node shows for the pool app. An Umbrel app answering with Umbrel's login page: "Umbrel keeps this app's pages behind its login, so i can't read the pool from here. updating the app may fix it; otherwise i can still catch a block from your payout address and read your miners if you give me their addresses." and offer: watch my address and miners (primary) / try the other route.

Save the pool as `pools[0]`, `role` primary, `pool` from detect (ckpool, braiins, sololuck, publicpool, atlas, gobrrr, nerdminers or ocean), `port` the miner's stratum port, `pool_url` the tested base URL for a home pool (null for a public pool). `stats` false only where stats can't be read at all. A backup goes in `pools[1]` the same way, `role` backup, a short `name` (like "home node 2"), `address` only if it pays a different one.

## 2. The rest, one at a time
1. Network data, one options card, "where should network data come from?": public mempool.space (default, no node details; it sends nothing about their address, just generic block reads) / my own mempool (its onion or Tailscale URL, saved as `mempool_url`) / my own bitcoin core node (read-only RPC). Only for the node, ask its RPC URL on the chosen route. Detect, don't list: reuse what runs their home pool, or a node name in the pasted address (umbrel, umbrel.local); else one open line, "what runs your node? just say it in your own words." Show ONLY the matching line:
   - Umbrel: open the Bitcoin Node app, tap Connect (top right), go to the RPC Details tab and pick Tor. it shows the .onion, port 8332, username and password. use the RPC .onion with port 8332, not the P2P one with 8333.
   - Start9 (StartOS 0.3.5): Services > Bitcoin Core > Interfaces > RPC Interface shows the Tor address; add :8332. username and password are in Config > RPC Settings, or scan the QuickConnect QR in Properties.
   - anything else: look for the node's RPC address or its Tor .onion in its settings or connect screen, port 8332.
   RPC username and password (Umbrel and Start9 ones too) go ONLY into one masked secret-request field saved as `SOLO_PLEB_RPC` as `user:password`, never in chat; say so here and save `rpc_user` null. Say in one line why it's safe: the script only allows getblockchaininfo, getblockcount, getbestblockhash, getblockhash, getblock and getblockheader, never wallet RPCs. With RPC it alerts when the node lags 3+ blocks and checks their address from the node if mempool.space is down. Be honest that Umbrel and Start9 hand out the node's main RPC login, which isn't read-only; a separate read-only rpcauth user is safer if they can make one. `public_fallback` true for mempool.space; for node or own mempool, ask if mempool.space may be a fallback (solo-pool block alerts and the daily/fee lines need a mempool).
2. Currency: one single-select card, "which currency?": USD (primary), EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, JPY, allowCustom on (CHF is typed). It must be a key of mempool.space `/api/v1/prices` (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, CHF, AUD, JPY), else ask again. Save as `currency`. Always asked, power or not: block and spendable cards show fiat next to every BTC value.
3. Power cost: one card, "add power cost (recommended)" / "skip" (it gives weekly power cost and J/TH). If added: typed watts per miner (AxeOS shows it; offer typical figures if unsure); a group total is split evenly, each with `"watts_est": true`; price per kWh in their currency (don't ask currency again). Then: "is that one price all day, or a cheaper rate at certain hours (like an overnight tariff)?" If it varies, save `tariff` {"default_kwh":<usual>,"bands":[{"from":"HH:MM","to":"HH:MM","kwh":<price>}]} in their timezone instead of `kwh_price` (cost is weighted by the hours each miner runs). Per miner save `worker` (after the dot in `stratumUser`) and its address, and ask how to reach it (onion or Tailscale for background checks, LAN for chat checks only). Reachable miners give live draw (AxeOS `/api/system/info`, or Avalon cgminer on 4028; 7-day average, "live avg"), else typed watts ("typed"); LAN-only miners are read from their registered computer when they ask in chat. Skipped: leave `watts` and `kwh_price` out; the power lines then never show, not even as zero. Expected value is shown as an average: most weeks pay nothing, one block pays everything.
4. Timezone: one open line, which city or timezone; save an IANA name (like `America/Chicago`) as `timezone`. Times show with its label ("15:42 CST"), daylight saving handled. Never assume one. They can change currency, kWh price, timers or timezone any time by telling me; I update config.json.
5. Timers, asked once, openly: "do any of your miners run on a timer or only at certain hours, like a cheap overnight rate? if so, which ones and when do they switch on and off?" Skip or "no" means 24/7. Save `schedules` {"<worker>": {"on": "HH:MM", "off": "HH:MM", "grace_min": 30, "start_grace_min": 45}} in their timezone. Switching off on schedule (or up to grace_min early) and on early or on time are silent; a drop while it should run is a normal down card; one "didn't come on" card if not seen start_grace_min after switch-on. If it switches off a bit early, offer a bigger grace rather than guessing. Its uptime counts its own window; 7-day average and odds use real hashrate.
6. Quiet hours, only if they ask to silence a miner at certain times: `quiet_hours` {"<worker>" or "*": "HH:MM-HH:MM"}. A drop inside sends nothing; one "still down after your quiet hours" card follows if it hasn't come back.
7. Alerts: cards don't pre-tick, so first one single-select card, "which alerts?": "recommended (block, 1 G, 1 T, all-time best, down/back, solo block)" (primary) / "let me choose". Recommended: write `possible_block`, `milestone_g`, `milestone_t`, `best_share`, `worker_quiet`, `recovery`, `solo_pool_block` all true. Only on "let me choose", one multiSelect card, "what should ping you?": block found (`possible_block`), a worker crosses 1 G (`milestone_g`), crosses 1 T (`milestone_t`), new all-time best (`best_share`), miner down / back (`worker_quiet` + `recovery`), solo-pool block anywhere (`solo_pool_block`); picked true, unpicked false. Either way: `failover` true with a backup (left out without), `watcher` true (my own health, on neither card), and `fees` false, with one line that fee alerts can be turned on later just by asking (then ask the threshold in sat/vB, offer 5). Node lag is automatic with RPC. Mutes go in `mutes` as {type: unix_until} for 4, 8 or 12 hours.

The script prints every alert as a markdown card; relay cards exactly as printed. What they mean, for explaining:
- block: only when a new block's coinbase pays their address, never a guess (a share above difficulty is a calm "possible block" line); later one "spendable" card at 100 confirmations or one honest "orphaned". Milestones climb 1 G, 1 T, block; one share never gets two cards.
- down / back: pool unreachable only after 2 failed checks; every down gets a back; miners dropping together share one card; "last seen", never "last share".
- backup: readable, a miner hashing there is not down and still counts, with "moved to backup" / "back on primary" cards; down only when silent on both. Unreadable: "may have failed over", unknown in uptime, never down.
- Public Pool hosted stats or AtlasPool silent 2 checks: one "can't read stats" card, then "stats back". mempool.space down 3 checks: one card, scans resume. A damaged state file is restored from the last good copy, said once.
- watcher: errors in scheduled runs are recorded, never half-saved, and the script exits cleanly; 3 failures of a kind in a row (weekly digest: the first) give one "watcher having trouble" card, then "watcher ok again". Chat runs (`status`, `sample`, `migrate`, `--dry`) never count and print "check couldn't finish" at once.
- block scan: each check reads every block since the last (up to 900, then "catching up"), for their address and solo-pool wins anywhere. Nothing is missed while the box sleeps; it only arrives later.

## 3. Write the files
`/workspace/solo-pleb/config.json` (no secrets, only the env var name):
```json
{"route":"hosted|tor|tailscale|lan",
 "pools":[{"role":"primary","address":"<payout address>","pool":"ckpool|braiins|sololuck|publicpool|atlas|gobrrr|nerdminers|ocean","port":3333,"pool_url":"http://<tested base URL, or null for a public pool>"},
          {"role":"backup","name":"<short name>","address":"<only if different>","pool":"ckpool","pool_url":null}],
 "node":{"rpc_url":null,"rpc_user":null,"rpc_secret_env":"SOLO_PLEB_RPC"},"mempool_url":null,"public_fallback":false,
 "miners":[{"model":"Bitaxe Gamma","hashrate_ths":1.2,"watts":18,"worker":"<worker name>","url":"http://<miner address>","reach":"tor|tailscale|lan"}],"currency":"<their pick>","kwh_price":0.15,"tariff":{"default_kwh":0.30,"bands":[{"from":"00:30","to":"04:30","kwh":0.09}]},
 "schedules":{"<worker on a timer>":{"on":"23:30","off":"05:30","grace_min":30,"start_grace_min":45}},"quiet_hours":{},
 "fee_threshold_satvb":5,"timezone":"<IANA zone, like America/Chicago>","alerts":{"possible_block":true,"milestone_g":true,"milestone_t":true,"best_share":true,"worker_quiet":true,"recovery":true,"solo_pool_block":true,"failover":true,"watcher":true,"fees":false},"mutes":{},"config_version":19}
```
Leave out: the backup entry and `failover` with no backup, `schedules` with no timers, `kwh_price`/`tariff`/`watts` when power is skipped (`tariff` only for time-of-day prices), `quiet_hours` unless asked. `"stats":false` only when a pool's stats can't be read at all. Older configs (no `port`, or a top-level `addresses` list, each a primary) still load.
Then, on first run, write the python from the `solo-pleb-check` skill's fenced block verbatim to `/workspace/solo-pleb/check.py` (state.json goes next to it), verify with `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('/workspace/solo-pleb/check.py').read())"`, and run it. Modes: `watch` (default, hourly), `fees`, `daily`, `weekly`, `status`, `sample` (example alerts, reads and saves nothing), `migrate` (section 0), `detect`. It prints nothing when nothing changed, else markdown cards separated by blank lines. `status` is read-only (never saves or uses up an alert; alerts come from `watch`); `--dry` runs any mode without saving. State saves atomically with a `state.json.bak` copy.

## 4. Prove it works
Run `python3 /workspace/solo-pleb/check.py status` once, live, and relay the card as printed (worker table, odds with working, network, pools, timers, downtime, and power only with watts). Add node sync if RPC is set. If the pool, node or onion didn't answer, say exactly which.

Then show an alert so the first real one isn't a surprise: run `python3 /workspace/solo-pleb/check.py sample` and relay it exactly as printed (sample down and backup cards with their own names, marked as samples; reads and saves nothing). Then one line: "that's only a sample. real ones arrive the same way, and only when something happens."

## 5. Routines
Say plainly that every routine run costs tokens even when it sends nothing, so more checks cost more. Offer miner-watch (hourly), weekly-digest (Monday 8am), daily-oneliner (9am) and fee-alert (every 30 min, off unless wanted). For miner-watch offer one token saver: hourly by day, every 2 hours overnight; be honest that every check scans every block since the last, so nothing is missed, alerts just arrive later. Resume each only after a yes. Same network only: no routines, checks happen in chat.
